source_pins.finding: OCI descriptors use collision-resistant digests as content identifiers; consumers can verify retrieved bytes against digest. OCI image manifests are designed for content-addressable images.
Statement subjects bind attestations to software artifacts by digest; subjects are assumed immutable and matched by digest.
Build provenance records verifiable information describing where, when and how artifacts were produced and is intended to let consumers verify expected build origin/process.

Artifact attestations cryptographically sign build provenance including repository/workflow/commit context and support digest-bound container subjects. Private-repository attestations use GitHub's Sigstore instance and do not use the public transparency log.

source_pins.source: Nix 2.31 reference manual + official NixOS CA-derivations documentation
source_pins.finding: Serialized derivations are content-addressed and a closure can be content-addressed when transitive inputs follow the common content-addressed case; CA derivations remain opt-in/experimental on the documented surface.

findings: A digest-bound OCI artifact can prevent a queued runtime probe from silently executing different bytes under the same mutable name/tag.
in-toto/SLSA can bind that artifact to build/source provenance and materials, reducing the gap between Git source identity and runtime artifact identity.
GitHub Artifact Attestations are a low-friction candidate for signing/verifying provenance when the build already runs in GitHub Actions.
Nix-style content-addressed closure is stronger as a hermetic/reproducible build model but is a heavier architectural dependency than F2 currently needs for this specific churn problem.

None of these mechanisms proves that an older runtime subject remains semantically representative after a newer F2 generation changes the same integration boundary. Content identity solves WHAT EXECUTED; it does not solve WHETHER THAT SUBJECT IS STILL CURRENT.
Therefore digest/provenance evidence must never mint RUNTIME_SUBJECT_INVARIANT or current-generation runtime credit by itself.
counterhypotheses: Git commit SHA alone may be sufficient if every runtime probe executes directly from a clean checkout with fully pinned dependencies and config; artifact attestation would then add complexity without changing correctness.
A full Nix/Guix-style hermetic build could reduce provenance ambiguity further, but its dependency/operational weight may exceed the value of a thin F2-native subject envelope.
Attestation infrastructure can authenticate a builder's claim without proving runtime execution; treating it as execution evidence would recreate the exact evidence inflation F2 forbids.

preferred_stack: OCI-style SHA-256 content identity for executable artifact when containerized
thin in-toto/SLSA-like provenance fields for source/build/material binding
optional GitHub Artifact Attestation verification where already available
do_not_promote: Nix/CA-derivations as mandatory F2 runtime dependency
artifact attestation as target-runtime execution evidence
digest equality as semantic-equivalence proof across F2 generations

next_exact_action: Acquire E2_ARCHITECTURE_MAPPED claim and map a minimal RuntimeSubjectAttestation envelope onto the existing F2 runtime-credit/receipt path without introducing a second ledger or acceptance authority.
